points.description: Correctly contrasts the two modes: asynchronous sends each character individually as a self-contained unit framed by start and stop bits (simple/cheap, low transmission rate), whereas synchronous groups many characters into a continuous stream/frames (delimited by SYN/flag), needing sender–receiver synchronization (more complex, higher rate). Equivalent wording accepted; the key required contrast is character-by-character with start/stop bits versus blocks/frames of characters. Extras like cost, complexity, speed, SYN/flag are optional.
